# Consumer acknowledgement

Q: What does acknowledging a message do?
A: The message is removed from that consumer's pending set. Relay will not deliver it
to that consumer again.

Q: Is acknowledgement required?
A: Yes. Until a message is acknowledged it stays pending for the consumer that
received it.

# Delivery ordering

Behaviour: Messages published by one producer are delivered to a consumer in the order
in which they were published.

Reason: Consumers rebuild state by replaying messages, and an out-of-order replay would
corrupt that state.

# Subscription lease

Q: How long does a subscription stay alive without a renewal?
A: A subscription expires unless the consumer renews it within 10 minutes of the
previous renewal.

# Delivery deadline

Behaviour: A message that has not been delivered within 24 hours of being published is
moved to the dead-letter store and is not delivered afterwards.

Reason: A message older than that is stale for every known consumer.

evidence.content:
# Consumer acknowledgement

Q: What does acknowledging a message do?
A: The message is removed from that consumer's pending set. Relay will not deliver it
to that consumer again. Acknowledging also releases the storage slot that was reserved
for the message while it was pending, so the slot can be reused by later messages.

Q: Is acknowledgement required?
A: Yes. Until a message is acknowledged it stays pending for the consumer that
received it.

# Delivery ordering

Behaviour: Messages published by one producer are delivered to a consumer in the order
in which they were published.

Behaviour: Ordering survives a redelivery. When a message from a producer is
redelivered, it is delivered before any message that the same producer published after
it.

Reason: Consumers rebuild state by replaying messages, and an out-of-order replay would
corrupt that state.

# Delivery receipts

Behaviour: Relay keeps a receipt for every delivery it makes. Receipts are kept for 14
days and are then discarded.

Reason: Operators investigate delivery disputes within two weeks; older receipts are
never consulted.

# Subscription lease

Q: How long does a subscription stay alive without a renewal?
A: A consumer must renew its subscription at least once every 600 seconds, measured
from the previous renewal; otherwise the subscription lapses.

# Delivery deadline

Behaviour: A message that has not been delivered within 48 hours of being published is
moved to the dead-letter store and is not delivered afterwards.

Reason: A message older than that is stale for every known consumer.

candidate.facet: What happens to a received message until and when it is acknowledged
candidate.subject: Consumer acknowledgement

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B1-T2 answers what acknowledgement does to a received message and that it stays pending until acknowledged, the same locus as ADDR-53ff2ec77ba59cb1.

candidate.facet: In what order are one producer's messages delivered to a consumer
candidate.subject: Message delivery

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B2-T2 states that one producer's messages are delivered in publish order and that this order survives redelivery, answering the same order question as ADDR-fae4d2447766ee14.
EV-LV-B2-T2 introduces receipts kept for every delivery and discarded after 14 days, a different subject and question from producer-to-consumer delivery order.

candidate.facet: How long it stays alive without renewal
candidate.subject: Subscription

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B3-T2 states the renewal interval after which a subscription lapses, matching ADDR-e2ce413edf45d95f.

candidate.facet: What happens if it is not delivered within a deadline
candidate.subject: Published message

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B4-T2 describes moving an undelivered published message to the dead-letter store after a deadline, matching ADDR-354966f9aaeb432c.
EV-LV-B1-T2 restates that acknowledgement removes the message from that consumer's pending set and Relay will not deliver it to that consumer again.
EV-LV-B1-T2 restates that until a message is acknowledged it stays pending for the consumer that received it.

value.text: Acknowledging releases the storage slot reserved for the message while it was pending, so the slot can be reused by later messages.

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B1-T2 adds a compatible acknowledgement effect: the reserved storage slot is released for reuse by later messages.
EV-LV-B2-T2 restates that messages published by one producer are delivered to a consumer in the order in which they were published.

value.text: When a message from a producer is redelivered, it is delivered before any message that the same producer published after it.

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B2-T2 adds that publication order survives redelivery, a compatible ordering proposition at this locus.
EV-LV-B2-T2 states that delivery receipts are kept for 14 days and are then discarded.
EV-LV-B3-T2 requires renewal at least every 600 seconds from the previous renewal, which is the same 10-minute lifetime without renewal.

value.text: A message that has not been delivered within 48 hours of being published is moved to the dead-letter store and is not delivered afterwards.

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-B4-T2 states that an undelivered message is dead-lettered after 48 hours of being published and is not delivered afterwards.

proposal.reason: EV-LV-B4-T2 replaces the 24-hour undelivered deadline with 48 hours, so the prior fate claim is no longer current.
